items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I was with Dinah Washington... I used to hook up her corset... I was traveling with her and our trio... I met all the bandleaders and all the people that we played with.

ctx.x: . . . but you couldn’t come in the front door and have a meal.

Like Las Vegas, where you could go in behind the bandstand and come up on the stage in the lounge, play, but you had to go back out – come back out. When I was with Dinah Washington, you had to do that and go – we had a trailer out in the parking lot. That’s before Frank Sinatra went out there and cooled all that out for Sammy Davis. But it was that kind of a thing. So we worked down in the Blue Mirror like that, but I don’t remember a lot of black people coming there. We worked two weeks there. For me that was…
Is a patch pocket like a Chesterfield?

items.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: They have been the propelling force behind some of the greatest jazz soloists, including Miles Davis, Cannonball Adderley, Dinah Washington and Dizzy Gillespie.

ctx.x: Bassist Walter Booker and drummer Jimmy Cobb, currently working with the Nat Adderley Quintet, make up one of the finest rhythm teams in jazz today.
They have been the propelling force behind some of the greatest jazz soloists, including Miles Davis, Cannonball Adderley, Dinah Washington and Dizzy Gillespie.
Walter and Jimmy were interviewed by Michael Woods on a Royal Caribbean
